https://telex.hu/kulfold/2026/09/01/mari.text: Menü Kereső Németország meg fogja kapni a megfelelő választ, üzenték az oroszok a konzulátust bezáró németeknek Külföld Marija Zaharova – Fotó: Nikita Shvetsov / Anadolu Agency / AFP Molnár Zoltán Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Németország „meg fogja kapni a megfelelő választ” arra a döntésére, hogy bezáratja a berlini Orosz Házat és a bonni orosz főkonzulátust – jelentette ki Marija Zaharova, az orosz külügyminisztérium szóvivője kedd este a TASZSZ hírügynökségnek. Az MTI szerint Zaharova arra reagált, hogy a német kormány bejelentette, szeptember 18-ig bezáratja a bonni orosz főkonzulátust és a Berlinben működő Orosz Ház kulturális központot, továbbá megszigorítja az orosz állampolgárok beutazásának ellenőrzését is. Ennek oka, hogy a német rendőrség Moszkvát tette felelőssé a lipcsei repülőtéren történt drónincidensért. „Az Orosz Ház és a bonni főkonzulátusunk egyaránt rég nem hagyta nyugton a [német] kormányzó elitet. Most kitaláltak egy ürügyet. Nos, akkor megkapják a méltó választ” – érvelt az orosz diplomata. Ugyanezen a napon közölte Alexander Dobrindt német belügyminiszter, hogy Oroszország megbízásából kísérelhették meg a támadást a lipcsei repülőtéren a robbanószerrel felszerelt drónnal, ami meghiúsult. Ezért Németország újabb Oroszország elleni büntetőintézkedéseket vezetett be, ezt Johann Wadephul német külügyminiszter is megerősítette. A közepes méretű drónon robbanószert is találtak , és az az ukránok hatalmas Antonov teherszállító gépe mellé, a reptér betonjára került. Az erről készült képek, videók az bejárták a világsajtót . Mark Rutte, a NATO főtitkára azt nyilatkozta, hogy a szervezet teljes mértékben szolidaritást vállal Németországgal. „A bizonyítékok egyértelműek. És üdvözlöm a Németország által válaszul bejelentett intézkedéseket” – írta az X-en. Eközben Emmanuel Macron francia elnök is kiállt Németország mellett az X-re kitett posztjában. Felidézte, hogy a németek megállapították Oroszország felelősségét a Lipcsében történtekben. Szerinte egyre több ilyen hibrid támadás történik Európában, ami nem maradhat válasz nélkül. „Franciaország teljes mértékben szolidaritást vállal Németországgal, és támogatja az Oroszország elleni új európai szankciók elfogadását” – írta az államfő. Szerinte az eszkalációval szemben egységesnek és határozottnak kell lenni, és meg kell erősíteni Ukrajna támogatását, amiből Franciaország kiveszi a részét. https://www.dw.com/en/trump-s-iran-strat.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5Kwzu A US fighter aircraft launches from an aircraft carrier in the Arabian Sea (FILE: August 2026) Image: U.S. Navy/Planet Pix/ZUMA/picture alliance Advertisement US President Donald Trump has given a fairly clear description of what the next phase of the Iran war could look like. The Iranians had tried to rebuild their radar equipment, Trump stated after the most recent wave of US strikes . "We waited until it was almost built, and then we hit it," he said. On Tuesday, American forces once again attacked several targets in Iran . According to US Central Command (CENTCOM), the targets destroyed included "air defense sites, radar systems, maritime assets and facilities, mine laying capabilities, and communications sites." 'Mowing the grass' Iran responded by firing rockets and drones at US facilities in the region. With this, the war moved on to what CENTCOM had indicated just a few days earlier could be the strategy for the next phase. What strategy will Donald Trump choose to pursue next in the war with Iran? Image: Ken Cedeno/REUTERS According to the news portal Axios, it was considering limited strikes, at regular intervals if necessary, to prevent Iran from reconstituting its military capabilities in the Strait of Hormuz . An American government representative used a concept from Israeli security policy to describe this idea: He called it "mowing the grass." The metaphor refers to a strategy that doesn't even attempt to promise that an opponent will be defeated once and for all. It is enough to regularly reduce the enemy's military capabilities to the point where the threat remains manageable. When the grass grows back, you "mow" it again. Applied to the situation in Iran, this would mean the US keeping an eye on which military capabilities the enemy is reconstituting, and attacking once it crosses a certain threshold. Successes that won't last In the past few months, the US has scored some military successes. US forces have significantly reduced Iran's military capabilities in the Strait of Hormuz, and have begun clearing Iranian sea mines. However, these successes will not last. Tehran is repairing or procuring new radar installations, anti-aircraft positions and anti-ship missiles. US bombs could certainly destroy important Iranian positions with targeted strikes. But the knowledge and the industrial basis of Iranian military technology would remain. This image issued by US CENTCOM shows a precision strike against an Iranian military target in July 2026 Image: US Central Command/AFP Reconstruction can therefore be delayed, but not prevented. The US will repeatedly be confronted with the same choice: whether to accept that Tehran is regaining its capabilities, or to attack again and destroy them. Mona Yacoubian, director of the Middle East program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies in Washington, warned as early as April that this development could lead to an "enduring low-intensity conflict punctuated by more intensive interventions." Trump's belligerent warnings The fact that the strategy of "mowing the grass" is reaching its limits is also because it was never designed for a war with a state. Israel developed the strategy to combat non-state actors like Hamas . However, as Yacoubian pointed out in her article, the Israeli academics who initially coined the term warned that if the opponent had "statist characteristics and/or more powerful capabilities, 'mowing the grass' might become an outdated military strategy." This is clearly the case with the Strait of Hormuz. The US needs to keep the strait reliably open. Iran, on the other hand, only needs to make people believe that the passage remains dangerous. In this way, even a significantly weakened opponent can impose substantial costs on Washington. Keeping the vital shipping lane through the Strait of Hormuz open is a priority for the US Image: Atta Kenare/AFP Another problem for the US is that, while Washington can determine the intensity of its own attacks, it has no control over Tehran's response. This week, Trump warned Tehran not to launch a retaliatory strike, threatening that Iran would be "totally wiped out as a country" if it did. Nonetheless, the regime in Tehran immediately fired missiles against American facilities in the region. Jordan alone reported 13 ballistic missiles in its airspace, 10 of which it was able to intercept. The nuclear question But Yacoubian believes that repeated American attacks carry a far greater risk. She warns that they may lead Tehran to conclude that " pursuit of a nuclear weapon " is the only way to achieve "lasting deterrence." This suggests that, by attacking Iran, the US and Israel could actually accelerate the precise development they sought to bring under control. The Natanz nuclear facility in Iran was one of the first sites targeted by the US and Israel Image: Planet Labs From Washington's perspective, the alternatives available to Trump don't look much better. If the president accepts Iran rebuilding its military strength around the Strait of Hormuz, he risks renewed attacks on shipping and disruption of one of the world's most important energy routes . The consequences for the global economy are well known. In spite of the upheaval and repeated negotiations , a political agreement between Washington and Tehran has so far failed because of apparently insurmountable differences. America's next 'forever war'? For Trump, "mowing the grass" has domestic appeal, in spite of the uncertainty it brings to foreign policy. The US president would be able to avoid occupation, nation building and deploying large numbers of American ground troops. At the same time, it allows him to distance himself from the so-called "forever wars" he repeatedly accused his predecessors in the White House of pursuing. Ultimately, though, this supposed way of avoiding a forever war could become one of its own. Yacoubian describes it as a "Sisyphean attrition strategy without end." As long as Washington is not prepared at some point to accept the rebuilding of Iran's capabilities, each successful attack merely creates the justification for the next one. This article has been translated from German. https://www.politico.eu/article/donald-t.text: DUBLIN — U.S. President Donald Trump waded into another age-old conflict Saturday, declaring on a golf-focused visit to Ireland that he’d like to see the island unified — the nightmare scenario for Northern Ireland’s British unionists. Sitting beside Irish Taoiseach Micheál Martin after an overnight flight from Washington, Trump said he couldn’t understand why Northern Ireland — the part of the island that remained in the U.K. when the rest of Ireland won independence over a century ago — hadn’t already joined the Republic of Ireland. “I’d love to see it unified. I think it’d be great. A great feather in everybody’s cap if that happened. It’s going to happen eventually,” Trump said, gesturing to Martin, who has spent years trying behind the scenes to build better relations with unionists, to little avail. “You’ve got the right man over here to get it moving. But I think it would be a fantastic thing. Now the U.K. will have something to say about it obviously. But I think it’d be a great thing. How can it be bad?” Advertisement Advertisement Nearly 3,700 people were killed in three decades of bloodshed over the constitutional future of Northern Ireland, a conflict largely settled by the U.S.-brokered Good Friday accord of 1998. Crucially, that peace deal specified that Northern Ireland should stay a separate part of the U.K. as long as most voters support this — a position unchanged, according to virtually all opinion polls, in the years since. Trump’s out-of-the-blue endorsement of Irish unity spurred an immediate rejection from Northern Ireland’s main pro-British party, the Democratic Unionists , who have been the island’s main supporters of Trump’s MAG A movement . “President Trump knows better than most that elections matter,” said Democratic Unionist leader Gavin Robinson. “Northern Ireland is part of the United Kingdom because that is the settled democratic will of its people,” Robinson wrote on X . “As unionists we are not interested in the destruction of our country by joining with the Irish Republic.” The Protestant unionist side of the community that once commanded a firm majority in Northern Ireland has been in seemingly terminal decline . Irish nationalists on the Catholic side of the divide, by contrast, have increasingly demanded a referendum on Irish unity following Britain’s exit from the European Union — a move that made it easier for Northern Ireland to trade goods with the Republic of Ireland, an EU member country, than with the rest of the United Kingdom. Advertisement Advertisement Sinn Féin, the Irish republican party that leads the cross-community government in Northern Ireland created by the 1998 peace deal, offered no immediate reaction. Sinn Féin, a staunch supporter of the Palestinian cause, has boycotted meetings with Trump since his 2024 election. But Sinn Féin’s moderate Irish nationalist rivals, the Social Democratic and Labour Party, offered a tongue-in-cheek welcome for Trump’s apparent endorsement of their position. SDLP leader Claire Hanna drew gasps and whoops from the audience at her party’s annual conference in Belfast when she declared: “Donald Trump in the last hour has announced that he is in favor of a united Ireland.” “Turns out he’s not as orange as he looks,” she said, referencing Trump’s facial make-up as well as the main Protestant fraternal organization in Northern Ireland, the Orange Order. Trump quickly acknowledged that his Irish unity remarks would raise eyebrows and make headlines. At a later appearance at the official residence of U.S. Ambassador to Ireland Edward Walsh, Trump led his remarks by noting he’d just told journalists that a united Ireland would “be a very cool thing.” “I gave a nice answer, I think. We’ll read about it tomorrow,” he said to laughter from the audience, which included many of Ireland’s political leaders and corporate kingpins. “There’s no good answer, right?” This article was updated. https://www.dw.com/en/us-justice-departm.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5O7f6 Trump has long been at odds with the mainstream media, regularly calling them 'fake news' [FILE: September 2026] Image: Alex Wroblewski/AFP Advertisement The US Department of Justice announced on Saturday that it is investigating whether the White House press pool 's decision to halt coverage of President Donald Trump last month, violated the nation's anti trust law. Group boycotts among business competitors might violate US law, spokesperson Emily Covington said. "The Antitrust Division is simply investigating to determine whether these news organizations have violated the antitrust laws," she said. The networks under the scrutiny are ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and Fox News. Jose Zamora, the Committee to Protect Journalists' regional director of the Americas, criticized the administration's decision to investigate. "The government should not use antitrust investigations to intimidate news outlets defending press access," Zamora said on X. "The public's right to know depends on that access." Under pressure — Trump's fractured America To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Why is Trump's press pool under investigation? On September 21, a pool of five broadcasters ceased presidential coverage after the Trump administration barred news networks CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, saying covering the president was a "privilege, not a right." Trump bans media outlets from White House To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video As a result, the five television networks suspended coverage in protest and refused to provide replacement program. The news outlets also sued the administration , accusing it of violating free speech and free press rights under the First Amendment of the US Constitution and pursuing retaliation over their coverage. On September 24, the White House reinstated their press credentials after a US district Judge ordered the administration to "immediately return, reinstate and restore" their access. The president has repeatedly called the mainstream media "fake news" and clashed with reporters during interviews. The White House press pool is a roating group of news outlets which cover the president and accompany him on official duties. CNN is one of the five news organizations, along with ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBS, that make up the primary White House television pool. They share the cost of covering the president and take turns organizing coverage and share the footage with outlets around the country. The White House press pool has now become a proxy for a fight over press freedom. Trump vs. the press: Who controls the story?
